motif.name: ATF3
evidence_context: Mouse marginal zone B cells; macrophage TLR4 response; colitis/UC
brief_interpretation: ATF3 drives PDL1 on mouse marginal zone B cells and restrains TLR-induced IL-6/IL-12b in macrophages; T-cell ATF3 protects against colitis.
biological_interpretation: ATF3 is a stress-inducible CREB/ATF bZIP factor. In mice fed a high-cholesterol diet, marginal zone B cells upregulated PDL1 in an ATF3-dependent manner, which limited T follicular helper cell accumulation and the germinal-center response (PMID 28414328). In TLR-activated macrophages ATF3 is induced by LPS and acts as a negative-feedback repressor of Il6 and Il12b transcription, as validated in Atf3-null mice (PMID 16688168). ATF3 expression in CD4+ T cells was inversely correlated with ulcerative colitis severity in patients, and T-cell-specific Atf3 deletion worsened DSS colitis through loss of Peyer's patch TFH cells, germinal centers and IgA (PMID 30862736).

motif.name: FOSL2::JUND(var.2)
evidence_context: Fra-2: mouse B-cell development; JunD: B-cell activation, human SLE B cells
brief_interpretation: Fra-2 (FOSL2) regulates mouse B-cell proliferation and differentiation; JunD is induced by BCR/CD40 signals and elevated in SLE patient B cells.
biological_interpretation: This JASPAR motif represents an AP-1 FOS-JUN heterodimer site; evidence is available for each component. Deletion of Fra-2 impaired B-cell proliferation in mouse bone marrow and pre-B to immature B differentiation, with Fra-2 directly enhancing Foxo1 and Irf4 transcription (PMID 28566276). In primary mouse B cells, both anti-Ig and CD40 ligand stimulation induced JunD mRNA and protein (PMID 7534795). JunD was upregulated in B cells from SLE patients and regulated B-cell proliferation, autophagy and immune function in knockdown/overexpression and mouse experiments (PMID 39220919).

motif.name: CREM
evidence_context: CD4 T cells in human SLE; NK cells
brief_interpretation: CREMalpha is elevated in SLE patient T cells and epigenetically controls IL2 and IL17A; CREM also restrains CAR/IL-15-driven NK-cell function.
biological_interpretation: CREM is a CREB/ATF-family bZIP factor recognising CRE sites. In human CD4+ T cells CREMalpha recruits DNMT3a to remodel the IL2 locus and reduces IL17A promoter methylation, and T cells from SLE patients express increased CREMalpha with a corresponding IL-2-low/IL-17A-high pattern (PMID 23019580). In NK cells, CREM is induced by CAR activation and IL-15 through PKA-CREB signalling, and its deletion enhanced CAR-NK effector function (PMID 40468083).

motif.name: CREB1
evidence_context: Mature B-cell BCR signalling (junB, bcl-2 induction); Th17/Treg autoimmunity
brief_interpretation: In mature B cells, BCR-induced CREB-1 phosphorylation drives junB and bcl-2 transcription through CRE elements; T-cell CREB promotes Th17-mediated autoimmunity.
biological_interpretation: In mature Bal17 B cells, membrane-Ig cross-linking activated the junB promoter through a CRE-like site occupied by CREB-1, which became phosphorylated on Ser133, and dominant-negative CREB blocked this response (PMID 8683108). In B-cell lines, anti-IgM or phorbol ester stimulation induced CREB Ser133 phosphorylation and CRE-dependent bcl-2 expression, linking CREB to B-cell activation and rescue from apoptosis (PMID 8816467). In T cells, CREB promotes Th17 differentiation by binding the Il17-Il17f locus and limits induced Treg survival; its deletion conferred resistance to autoimmune disease and colitis in mice (PMID 29050947).

motif.name: Creb5
evidence_context: Mouse asthma model; lung CD11b- dendritic cells
brief_interpretation: Creb5 was identified as a shared regulon in lung CD11b- dendritic cells during mouse asthma exacerbation, and Creb5 siRNA attenuated exacerbation.
biological_interpretation: CREB5 (CRE-BPa) is a CREB/ATF bZIP factor. In a house-dust-mite mouse asthma model challenged with allergens or RSV, single-cell RNA-seq with SCENIC analysis identified Creb5 as a regulon shared between exacerbation conditions with increased activity in CD11b- dendritic cells, and Creb5 siRNA attenuated HDM-, cockroach- and RSV-induced exacerbation (PMID 36038770).

motif.name: FOSL1::JUN(var.2)
evidence_context: Fra-1: B-cell activation, plasma-cell differentiation, rheumatoid-factor autoantibodies; c-Jun: B-cell activation in knockout mice
brief_interpretation: Fra-1 (FOSL1) restrains plasma-cell differentiation and rheumatoid-factor production in mouse B cells; c-Jun-deficient B cells proliferate and secrete Ig normally.
biological_interpretation: This motif represents an AP-1 FOS-JUN heterodimer site; evidence is available for each component. Fra1 is up-regulated upon B-cell activation, where it enhances activation-induced cell death; B-cell-specific Fra1 deletion enhanced plasma-cell differentiation and antibody responses, whereas Fra1 overexpression repressed Blimp1 and blocked plasma-cell differentiation (PMID 25288397). Fra1 deficiency in B cells also increased IgG1 bone-marrow plasma cells, IgG rheumatoid-factor production and autoimmune bone loss after immunization (PMID 30779858). c-Jun-deficient B cells from chimeric mice showed normal proliferation and immunoglobulin secretion (PMID 7889400).

motif.name: FOSL2::JUN(var.2)
evidence_context: Fra-2: mouse B-cell development; c-Jun: B-cell activation
brief_interpretation: Fra-2 (FOSL2) promotes mouse B-cell proliferation and pre-B differentiation via Foxo1/Irf4; c-Jun-deficient B cells proliferate and secrete Ig normally.
biological_interpretation: This motif represents an AP-1 FOS-JUN heterodimer site; evidence is available for each component. Fra-2 deletion impaired B-cell proliferation in bone marrow and the large pre-B to small pre-B/immature B transition, and Fra-2 enhanced transcription of Foxo1, Irf4, Ikaros and Aiolos (PMID 28566276). A review of AP-1 in plasma-cell biology describes Fra-1-, Fra-2- and B-ATF-containing complexes as central to B-cell development and plasma-cell differentiation (PMID 34066181). c-Jun-deficient B cells from chimeric mice showed normal proliferation and immunoglobulin secretion (PMID 7889400).

motif.name: ATF7
evidence_context: Macrophage innate immune memory; ulcerative colitis epithelium
brief_interpretation: ATF7 represses innate-immune genes in macrophages via G9a and mediates LPS-induced innate memory; ATF7 is reduced in ulcerative colitis mucosa.
biological_interpretation: ATF7 is a CREB/ATF bZIP factor closely related to ATF2. In macrophages ATF7 recruits the H3K9 methyltransferase G9a to suppress innate-immunity genes; LPS induces p38-dependent ATF7 phosphorylation and release from chromatin, producing long-lasting increases in basal target-gene expression and pathogen resistance (PMID 26322480). In ulcerative colitis patients, ATF7 expression in colonic mucosa was reduced and inversely correlated with disease severity, and epithelial ATF7 directly activates PINK1 to maintain mitophagy and limit colitis in mice (PMID 40586859).

motif.name: ATF2
evidence_context: Murine B-lymphoma cell line A20; TNF promoter regulation
brief_interpretation: ATF-2 and Jun bind the composite kappa3/CRE element of the TNF promoter in A20 B cells, a gene rapidly induced after BCR or CD40 stimulation.
biological_interpretation: ATF2 is a CREB/ATF bZIP factor that heterodimerises with Jun proteins. TNF is one of the earliest genes transcribed after B-cell stimulation through the antigen receptor or CD40 (PMID 8816436). In the murine B-cell lymphoma line A20, ATF-2 and Jun bound the composite kappa3/CRE site of the TNF promoter, whereas NFATp acted through a separate -76 site, a B-cell-specific arrangement that differs from T cells (PMID 8816436).

motif.name: JUN
evidence_context: B-cell TNF promoter (A20 cell line); c-jun-deficient B cells; human SLE genetic association
brief_interpretation: Jun binds the TNF promoter with ATF-2 in A20 B cells; c-Jun-deficient mouse B cells activate normally; a JUN SNP associates with SLE in Chinese.
biological_interpretation: c-Jun is a core AP-1 subunit. In the murine A20 B-cell lymphoma line, ATF-2 and Jun bound the composite kappa3/CRE element of the TNF promoter, a gene rapidly induced after BCR or CD40 stimulation (PMID 8816436). c-Jun-deficient B cells generated in RAG-2-deficient chimeric mice showed normal proliferation and immunoglobulin secretion after stimulation, with other Jun family members contributing most AP-1 activity in lymphocytes (PMID 7889400). In a Chinese case-control study (502 SLE patients, 652 controls), the c-Jun polymorphism rs3748814 was associated with SLE susceptibility (PMID 22489574).

motif.name: ELK1
evidence_context: Human naive B cells; IL-2-driven plasma-cell differentiation
brief_interpretation: In human naive B cells, IL-2 signals through ERK/ELK1 to repress BACH2 and commit activated cells to plasma-cell differentiation.
biological_interpretation: ELK1 is an ETS-family ternary complex factor activated by ERK MAP kinases. In human naive B cells stimulated in vitro, IL-2 signalling through the ERK/ELK1 pathway timed the repression of BACH2, which directed plasma-cell lineage commitment and IgM secretion (PMID 29129929). An active regulatory region within the BACH2 super-enhancer was under ELK1 control and differentially regulated upon B-cell activation and division (PMID 29129929). This links ELK1 to T-cell-help-dependent fate decisions in the same naive B-cell population studied here.

evidence_context: Spermatogenesis (mouse knockout)
brief_interpretation: No clear immune evidence found.
biological_interpretation: CREB3L4 (AIbZIP) is an ER-membrane-bound CREB3-family bZIP factor. Creb3l4 is expressed at low levels in most mouse organs and highly in postmeiotic male germ cells, and Creb3l4-deficient mice are healthy with reduced sperm numbers (PMID 16107712).

motif.name: JUNB(var.2)
evidence_context: Primary B-cell BCR/CD40 activation; Th17 autoimmunity model
brief_interpretation: JunB is synthesised de novo after BCR cross-linking and forms most AP-1 activity in primary B cells; it is induced by both BCR and CD40.
biological_interpretation: Resting primary mouse B cells lack detectable AP-1 binding; surface-Ig cross-linking induces de novo JunB synthesis within 2 h, and JunB is the main component of the induced B-cell AP-1 complexes (PMID 7923384). Both anti-Ig and CD40 ligand induce JunB mRNA and protein in primary B cells, through PKC-dependent and PKC-independent pathways respectively (PMID 7534795). In CD4 T cells, JunB is required for Th17 differentiation, and Junb-deficient mice are resistant to experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (PMID 29234109).

The BCL-6 zinc-finger domain interacts with c-Jun, JunB and JunD and represses AP-1-mediated transcription, through which BCL-6 represses the Blimp-1 promoter that controls plasma-cell differentiation (PMID 12165517).

evidence_context: Primary B-cell BCR versus CD40 signalling

motif.name: Pax2
evidence_context: PAX2/5/8 paired-box subfamily; PAX5 in B-cell identity
brief_interpretation: No clear immune evidence found.
biological_interpretation: PAX2 is a paired-box transcription factor that functions in kidney and nervous-system development. It belongs to the PAX2/5/8 subfamily, whose members share closely related paired-domain binding sites. The B-cell member of this subfamily is PAX5, which commits lymphoid progenitors to the B lineage and maintains B-cell identity and function through the mature stage (PMID 17440452; the reference concerns PAX5).

motif.name: ELK3
evidence_context: Human pro-B regulon; macrophage LPS response; ILC3 differentiation
brief_interpretation: An ELK3 regulon is enriched in human pro-B cells; in macrophages ELK3 is an LPS-repressed repressor that limits NOS2 expression and phagocytosis.
biological_interpretation: ELK3 (Net/Erp/Sap-2a) is an ETS-family ternary complex factor that acts mainly as a repressor. A multi-omic atlas of eight human B-cell precursor populations identified a putative ELK3 regulon enriched in pro-B cells and associated with cell-cycle progression (PMID 41071881). In mouse macrophages, Elk-3 repressed NOS2 promoter activity and was down-regulated by LPS before NOS2 induction (PMID 12896968), and Elk-3 overexpression reduced bacterial phagocytosis while its LPS-induced decrease was mediated in part by KLF4 (PMID 25351511).

motif.name: CREB3
evidence_context: Dendritic-cell maturation; monocyte chemokine receptor signalling
brief_interpretation: CREB3 (LUMAN/LZIP) is activated by intramembrane proteolysis during dendritic-cell maturation and binds CCR1 to enhance Lkn-1-induced chemotaxis.
biological_interpretation: CREB3 is an ER-membrane-anchored bZIP factor activated by regulated intramembrane proteolysis. LUMAN/CREB3 is endogenously expressed by dendritic cells, interacts with DC-STAMP in the ER, and is proteolytically activated upon DC maturation induced by various stimuli (PMID 20546900). Human LZIP binds the chemokine receptor CCR1 and enhanced Lkn-1-induced chemotaxis without affecting other CCR1 ligands (PMID 15001559).

motif.name: FLI1
evidence_context: Naive B-cell proliferation; murine lupus models
brief_interpretation: Reduced Fli-1 lowers mitogen-induced naive B-cell proliferation and, in lupus-prone mice, reduces activated B cells, autoantibodies and nephritis.
biological_interpretation: FLI1 is an ETS-family transcription factor. Fli-1-deficient naive B cells from lupus-prone and control mice showed reduced proliferative responses to several mitogens without changes in BCR, TLR4 or TLR9 expression, and transgenic Fli-1 overexpression causes an SLE-like disease (PMID 18692443). Fli-1 heterozygous NZM2410 lupus mice had lower anti-dsDNA autoantibodies, fewer total and activated splenic B cells, less proteinuria and nephritis, and improved survival (PMID 20731671). Increased Fli-1 mRNA has been reported in peripheral blood lymphocytes from lupus patients (PMID 20731671).

motif.name: ELF2
evidence_context: B-cell gene promoters (blk, lyn); early B/T lymphocyte development
brief_interpretation: ELF2/NERF-2 transactivates the B-cell blk and lyn promoters and cooperates with AML1; Elf2 isoforms perturb pre-B development in mice.
biological_interpretation: ELF2 (NERF) is an ETS factor related to ELF-1, cloned from human spleen and co-expressed in B and T cells; its NERF-2 isoform activates the lyn and blk promoters, and all isoforms bind ETS sites in blk, lck, lyn, mb-1 and immunoglobulin heavy-chain genes (PMID 8756667). NERF-2 physically interacts with AML1 (RUNX1) to cooperatively transactivate the B-cell-specific blk promoter, whereas the NERF-1a isoform represses it (PMID 14970218). In a mouse bone-marrow reconstitution model, Elf2a or Elf2b expression perturbed the pre-B stage and T-cell development while steady-state mature B cells were unaffected (PMID 28351373).

motif.name: ATF6
evidence_context: ER-stress response; antibody-secreting B-cell differentiation
brief_interpretation: ATF6 is an ER-stress-activated transcription factor, but ATF6alpha is not required for mouse B cells to become antibody-secreting cells.

motif.name: MNT
evidence_context: T-cell-specific deletion; CD4 Th1 skewing; inflammation
brief_interpretation: Mnt deletion in mouse T cells caused Th1-skewed CD4 hyperproliferation, intestinal inflammation and lymphoma, linking MNT to T-cell homeostasis.
biological_interpretation: MNT is a MAX-interacting E-box repressor that antagonizes MYC; the E-box motif is shared with MYC/MAX family members. Conditional deletion of Mnt in mouse T cells increased thymocyte apoptosis, disrupted T-cell development and immune homeostasis, skewed cytokine production toward Th1 with enhanced proliferation of activated CD4+ T cells, and led to intestinal inflammation, liver necrosis and T-cell lymphoma. A follow-up study showed that the dominant physiological role of Mnt in T cells is suppression of apoptosis, and that Mnt is required for Myc-driven T-cell proliferative expansion. These data place MNT within the MYC network that controls T-cell proliferation and survival.

motif.name: CENPB
evidence_context: Centromeric alpha-satellite binding; autoantigen in PBC
brief_interpretation: CENP-B binds the CENP-B box in centromeric alpha-satellite DNA and is a major anti-centromere autoantigen, including in primary biliary cholangitis.
biological_interpretation: CENP-B is a centromere protein that binds the 17-bp CENP-B box in human alpha-satellite (alphoid) DNA and organizes centromeric chromatin; its motif therefore corresponds to a repetitive centromeric sequence. Its documented link to immunity is as an autoantigen: purified CENP-B reacts with anti-centromere sera from patients with autoimmune disease, and antibodies to recombinant CENP-B were detected in 60% of ANA-positive primary biliary cirrhosis (cholangitis) sera and in none of 181 healthy sera. In T cells, the HTLV-1 bZIP factor HBZ binds CENP-B and abrogates its binding to alpha-satellite DNA, inhibiting CENP-B-mediated H3K9 trimethylation.

motif.name: ELF5
evidence_context: Epithelium-specific ETS factor; pediatric asthma association
brief_interpretation: ELF5 is an epithelium-restricted ETS factor; an ELF5 upstream SNP was associated with pediatric asthma (p = 0.043) in a Taiwanese cohort.
biological_interpretation: ELF5 is an ETS transcription factor expressed exclusively in epithelial cells, where it regulates lung epithelial specification and differentiation. Genetic evidence linking ELF5 to immune-mediated disease is limited to the EHF-ELF5 region on 11p13: in Taiwanese children, SNP rs3910901 upstream of ELF5 was associated with asthma (p = 0.043), and the association was diluted after adjustment for allergy comorbidity.

motif.name: ELF3
evidence_context: IL-17A/TNF-induced mediator in RA synovial fibroblasts; inflammatory ETS factor
brief_interpretation: ELF3 mediates IL-17A plus TNF synergy in RA synovial fibroblasts and is induced by inflammatory cytokines and LPS via NF-kappaB.
biological_interpretation: ELF3 (ESE-1) is an epithelium-enriched ETS factor whose GGAA motif overlaps that of ETS factors expressed in T cells. In synovial fibroblasts from RA patients, the combination of IL-17A and TNF, cytokines produced by Th17 and other immune cells, strongly induced ELF3 through NF-kappaB, C/EBPbeta and IkappaBzeta, and ELF3 depletion attenuated induction of cytokines and matrix metalloproteinases. Earlier work showed that ESE-1 is induced by inflammatory cytokines and LPS in vascular cells and monocyte-macrophages, binds NF-kappaB p50 and transactivates the NOS2 promoter.

motif.name: MTF1
evidence_context: RA risk-SNP-linked TF in activated synovial fibroblasts; thymic lymphoma susceptibility
brief_interpretation: MTF1 is linked to an RA risk SNP by 3D contact, its motif marks cytokine-induced synovial fibroblast super-enhancers, and its inhibition ameliorated mouse arthritis.
biological_interpretation: MTF1 is the metal-responsive transcription factor that induces metallothioneins and other zinc-responsive genes. In an integrative multi-omics study of RA, an RA risk SNP (rs28411362) in a cytokine-induced super-enhancer of synovial fibroblasts contacted the MTF1 promoter, the MTF1 binding motif was enriched in stimulation-specific super-enhancers, and MTF1 inhibition suppressed cytokine and chemokine production by synovial fibroblasts and ameliorated a mouse arthritis model. In mice, Mtf-1 variant alleles that differ in metal responsiveness determine susceptibility to radiation-induced thymic lymphoma.

motif.name: MLXIPL
evidence_context: Glucose-sensing ChREBP-HIF-1alpha axis limiting Th1 in CD4 T cells
brief_interpretation: In mouse CD4 T cells, ChREBP (MLXIPL) drives high-glucose-induced Hif-1alpha transcription, limiting IFN-gamma/Th1 responses in diabetic kidney disease.
biological_interpretation: MLXIPL encodes ChREBP, a glucose-sensing bHLH-ZIP transcription factor that binds carbohydrate response elements (E-box-like) with MLX. In mouse CD4+ T cells, culture in high glucose increased Hif-1alpha expression in a ChREBP-dependent manner, and a ChREBP-binding sequence in the Hif-1alpha promoter mediated this upregulation. Adoptive transfer of Chrebp-deficient CD4+ T cells into diabetic mice caused severe renal damage that depended on IFN-gamma, mirroring the effect of T-cell Hif-1alpha deletion. This links MLXIPL to nutrient sensing and Th1 restraint in CD4 T cells, and connects it to the HIF-1 motifs also enriched in this cell type.

motif.name: ARNT::HIF1A
evidence_context: HIF-1alpha/ARNT in Th17/Treg balance; ARNT partner competition in human CD4 T cells
brief_interpretation: HIF-1alpha and its partner ARNT regulate CD4 fate; in human CD4 T cells hypoxic HIF-1alpha outcompetes AhR for ARNT, promoting Th17 responses.
biological_interpretation: This motif represents the HIF-1 heterodimer of HIF-1alpha and ARNT (HIF-1beta). For HIF1A, T-cell HIF-1alpha deficiency in mice reduced Th17 and increased Treg differentiation and protected against Th17-dependent EAE, with HIF-1 transactivating RORgammat and targeting Foxp3 for degradation. For ARNT, which also partners with AhR, T-cell-specific Arnt deletion in mice left thymic development and TCR responses intact but abolished TCDD-induced thymic involution. In CD4+ T cells from allergic rhinitis patients and healthy controls, hypoxia increased HIF-1alpha, which outcompeted AhR for ARNT binding, blunting AhR-ligand suppression of Th17 responses and AhR-induced IL-10.

motif.name: HIF1A
evidence_context: CD4 Th17/Treg differentiation; experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis
brief_interpretation: HIF-1alpha links metabolic sensing to CD4 fate, promoting Th17 over Treg differentiation; T-cell HIF-1alpha loss protects mice from EAE.
biological_interpretation: HIF-1alpha is an oxygen- and metabolism-sensing transcription factor whose hypoxia-response-element motif is shared with HIF-2alpha/ARNT complexes. HIF-1 enhances Th17 development by transactivating RORgammat and cooperating with RORgammat and p300 at the IL-17 promoter, while binding Foxp3 and targeting it for proteasomal degradation, under both normoxic and hypoxic conditions. Independently, HIF-1alpha induction downstream of mTOR drives the glycolytic program required for Th17 differentiation, and its loss enhances Treg differentiation. In both studies, mice lacking HIF-1alpha in T cells were protected from Th17-mediated autoimmune neuroinflammation (EAE), a model of multiple sclerosis.

motif.name: JUND(var.2)
evidence_context: AP-1 regulation of T-cell proliferation and Th1/Th2 cytokines
brief_interpretation: JunD restrains T-cell proliferation and Th cytokine output; JunD-deficient T cells hyperproliferate and Th1 cells produce more IFN-gamma.
biological_interpretation: JUND is an AP-1 bZIP factor that binds TRE/CRE-like sites shared with other Jun and Fos family members. In mice, broad JunD overexpression reduced peripheral lymphocyte numbers, and transgenic T cells proliferated poorly with reduced IL-4, CD25 and CD69. Conversely, JunD-deficient T cells hyperproliferated after mitogen stimulation, JunD-deficient Th2 cells secreted more IL-4 and IL-10, and Th1-polarized JunD-deficient CD4+ T cells produced more IFN-gamma with increased T-bet and decreased SOCS-1. JunD thus acts as a brake on T-cell proliferation and as a regulator of Th1 and Th2 cytokine expression.

motif.name: ELF1
evidence_context: TCR zeta (CD3zeta) transcription in SLE T cells; SLE GWAS locus in Asians
brief_interpretation: ELF1 drives CD3zeta transcription in human T cells; defective active ELF1 underlies low CD3zeta in SLE, and ELF1 is an Asian SLE risk locus.
biological_interpretation: ELF1 is an ETS factor involved in T-cell development and function that, after phosphorylation and O-glycosylation, translocates to the nucleus as a 98-kDa form and transactivates the TCR zeta (CD3zeta) promoter. In T cells from most SLE patients the functional 98-kDa ELF1 form is reduced or altered, explaining decreased CD3zeta expression. Increased PP2A in lupus T cells dephosphorylates ELF1 at Thr-231, reducing its binding to the CD3zeta and FcRgamma promoters, and silencing PP2A restored CD3zeta expression and early TCR signaling. A GWAS in Hong Kong Chinese with replication in two other Asian populations identified ELF1 as an SLE susceptibility locus (rs7329174, OR 1.26).

motif.name: TFAP2C(var.2)
evidence_context: Keratinocyte TF in psoriasis-like inflammation with Th17/Th1 readouts
brief_interpretation: TFAP2C is elevated in psoriatic skin; its suppression reduced keratinocyte inflammation and Th17/Th1 activation in imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like mice.
biological_interpretation: TFAP2C (AP-2gamma) is an AP-2 family transcription factor, and its motif is shared with TFAP2A and TFAP2B. In psoriasis, TFAP2C expression was elevated in lesional skin, and TFAP2C silencing suppressed proliferation and inflammatory responses of cytokine-stimulated HaCaT keratinocytes. In the imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like mouse model, TFAP2C inhibition alleviated skin injury and reduced Th17 and Th1 cell activation, with TFAP2C acting through transcriptional activation of TEAD4.

motif.name: JUN
evidence_context: AP-1 in human CD4 IL-10 induction, IL-2 transcription and T-cell exhaustion
brief_interpretation: c-Jun is required for IL-12-induced IL-10 in human memory CD4 T cells, coactivates IL-2 transcription, and its overexpression counters CAR T-cell exhaustion.
biological_interpretation: c-Jun is the canonical AP-1 factor, binding TRE sites shared with JUND, JUNB and Fos/ATF partners. In human memory CD4+ T cells, IL-12 inactivated GSK3beta and increased c-Jun, and siRNA silencing of c-Jun abrogated IL-12-induced IL-10 production. The TCR-induced coactivator Schnurri-3/KRC physically associates with c-Jun and augments AP-1-dependent IL-2 gene transcription in T cells. In human CAR T cells, exhaustion was associated with increased AP-1 motif accessibility and reduced IL-2, and c-Jun overexpression enhanced expansion and function and diminished terminal differentiation.

motif.name: DBP
evidence_context: Circadian PAR-bZIP factor activating Il9 in Th9 differentiation
brief_interpretation: DBP activates Il9 transcription downstream of TGF-beta/IL-4-induced Smad3 linker phosphorylation, promoting Th9 differentiation in mouse and human CD4 T cells.
biological_interpretation: DBP is a circadian clock output PAR bZIP transcription factor, and its motif is shared with the related PAR bZIP factors HLF and TEF and with NFIL3. In Th9 differentiation driven by IL-4 and TGF-beta, phosphorylation of Smad3 at linker Ser213 via p38 is required for Il9 transcription, and DBP acts as an activator and E2F8 as a repressor of Il9 transcription through this pathway. siRNA knockdown of Dbp or E2f8 in Th9 cells promoted or suppressed tumor growth, respectively, in mouse tumor models, and DBP and E2F8 showed the same opposing functions in human Th9 differentiation in vitro. Th9 cells have been implicated in allergy and asthma.

motif.name: POU3F1
evidence_context: Interferon-induced in mouse macrophages; motif-predicted regulator in SLE CD4+ T cells
brief_interpretation: POU3F1 (Oct-6) is interferon-inducible in mouse macrophages and was among top predicted TFs for chromatin changes in SLE CD4+ T cells.
biological_interpretation: POU3F1 (Oct-6/SCIP/Tst-1) is a POU-domain octamer-binding transcription factor best characterised in Schwann cells. In mouse fibroblasts and macrophages, Oct-6 was induced by type I and type II interferon, mainly through STAT1, and contributed to dsRNA-induced transcriptional responses. In an ATAC-seq and RNA-seq study of peripheral CD4+ T cells from SLE patients, POU3F1 was one of the top five TFs predicted from differentially accessible regions overlapping differentially expressed genes. Octamer-type motifs can also be bound by other POU factors such as POU2F1 and POU2F2.

motif.name: TEF
evidence_context: Hematolymphoid progenitor survival and proliferation; TCF3::TEF fusion in B-ALL
brief_interpretation: TEF, a circadian PAR-bZIP factor, is expressed in hematolymphoid progenitors, where it blocks apoptosis and restrains proliferation.
biological_interpretation: TEF is a PAR-domain bZIP transcription factor of the circadian output network that shares its DNA-binding specificity with HLF and DBP. In mouse hematopoiesis, TEF was expressed in a small fraction of each hematolymphoid progenitor subset; ectopic TEF protected IL-3-dependent FL5.12 cells from apoptosis after IL-3 withdrawal and almost completely down-regulated the common beta chain of cytokine receptors, so cells accumulated in G0/G1. A TCF3::TEF gene fusion was identified in a pediatric B-lymphoblastic leukemia case.

motif.name: ZBTB33
evidence_context: T-cell chemokine migration (Jurkat); methyl-CpG repression in lupus-prone mouse CD4+ T cells; germinal centres
brief_interpretation: Kaiso partners with RhoH in T-cell chemokine responses and represses methylated Ctse in CD4+ T cells, with reduced binding in lupus-prone mice.
biological_interpretation: ZBTB33 (Kaiso) is a POZ-zinc-finger transcription factor that binds methylated CpG-containing DNA as well as a sequence-specific Kaiso binding site. In Jurkat T cells, Kaiso formed a complex with the hematopoietic GTPase RhoH and p120 catenin; Kaiso knockdown altered chemokine-induced migration and actin polymerisation, and Kaiso relocated to the nucleus after chemokine stimulation or TCR activation in a RhoH-dependent manner. In CD4+ T cells of lupus-prone MRL/lpr mice, Kaiso binding to a hypomethylated mCGCG site in Cathepsin E (Ctse) intron 1 was reduced and Ctse expression increased, and Ctse knockdown in EL4 cells lowered IL-10 secretion. Kaiso knockout mice showed splenomegaly and enlarged germinal centres with derepressed Bcl6.

motif.name: Creb5
evidence_context: Classical-monocyte regulon in human PBMC; monocyte TF driver in RA synovium
brief_interpretation: CREB5 regulon activity marks human classical monocytes, and CREB5 ranked among monocyte TF drivers distinguishing RA from osteoarthritis synovium.
biological_interpretation: CREB5 (CRE-BPa) is a CREB/ATF-family bZIP transcription factor; the MA0840.1 CRE-type motif is shared with other CREB/ATF members. Single-cell regulon analysis of healthy human PBMC found CREB5 regulon activity enriched in classical monocytes compared with nonclassical monocytes. In RA synovial tissue transcriptomes, network-based ranking placed CREB5 with RFX5 and IRF9 in the single TF-driver cluster that accounted for the main RA-versus-control differences in monocytes.

motif.name: HES1
evidence_context: Notch target in early thymocyte and human T-cell development; tested in mouse CD8+ effector differentiation
brief_interpretation: HES1 is required for early thymocyte expansion and human T-cell development, but was dispensable for mouse CD8+ short-lived effector cell differentiation.
biological_interpretation: HES1 is a bHLH transcriptional repressor and a canonical Notch target gene. Hes1-null fetal liver cells failed to generate mature T cells in RAG2-null hosts, with arrest at the CD4-CD8- double-negative stage and defective TCR-independent and TCR-dependent thymocyte expansion. In human CD34+ hematopoietic progenitors, HES1 maintained a quiescent stem-cell signature and repressed NK and myeloid differentiation, and HES1 knockdown reduced human T-cell development. In mouse CD8+ T-cell responses, HES1 deficiency did not affect short-lived effector cell differentiation, and Notch did not act through the HES1-PTEN axis in that setting.

motif.name: CREB1
evidence_context: TCR-induced CREB phosphorylation; CREB1-Notch2 control of CD8+ cytotoxic differentiation; CREB in Th17/Treg autoimmunity
brief_interpretation: TCR engagement phosphorylates CREB, and CREB1 cooperates with Notch2 at the granzyme B promoter to promote CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell differentiation.
biological_interpretation: CREB1 is a cAMP-responsive bZIP transcription factor whose CRE motif is shared with other CREB/ATF family members. CREB is unphosphorylated in resting T cells, and TCR engagement induces rapid Ser133 phosphorylation through a pathway involving Lck, PKC, Ras, Raf-1, MEK and RSK2. In mouse CD8+ T cells, the Notch2 intracellular domain bound phosphorylated CREB1 and the coactivator p300 on the granzyme B promoter, and Notch2-deficient T cells showed impaired differentiation into cytotoxic T lymphocytes. motif.name: HINFP
evidence_context: Histone H4 gene transcription, cell-cycle-coupled DNA replication and genome stability
brief_interpretation: No clear immune evidence found.
biological_interpretation: HINFP (HiNF-P) is a zinc-finger transcription factor required for histone H4 gene transcription, linking histone synthesis to DNA replication. Conditional ablation of Hinfp in mammalian cells depleted histone H4, increased nucleosome spacing, impeded DNA synthesis, altered chromosome complement and caused replicative stress and genomic instability.

motif.name: GATA6
evidence_context: Resident peritoneal macrophage identity, renewal and survival; myeloid reprogramming of progenitors
brief_interpretation: GATA6 controls identity, proliferative renewal and survival of resident peritoneal macrophages.
biological_interpretation: GATA6 is a zinc-finger GATA factor; its GATA motif is shared with other family members, including GATA3. Among hematopoietic cells, Gata6 is selectively expressed in mouse resident peritoneal macrophages, where myeloid Gata6 deletion altered the macrophage transcriptome, dysregulated proliferative renewal, delayed resolution of inflammation and increased cell death, partly via aspartoacylase. Aberrant Gata6 expression in hematopoietic progenitors of Max41 transgenic mice ablated the common lymphoid progenitor compartment and promoted myelopoiesis through PU.1 and C/EBPa, while T- and NK-cell development proceeded relatively normally.

motif.name: ATF6
evidence_context: UPR in cytotoxic CD8αβ+ intraepithelial lymphocytes in mouse TNF-driven Crohn's-like ileitis
brief_interpretation: ATF6 and other UPR components are increased in cytotoxic CD8αβ+ intraepithelial lymphocytes in mouse TNF-driven Crohn's-like ileitis.
biological_interpretation: ATF6 is an ER-membrane-anchored bZIP transcription factor and one of the three arms of the unfolded protein response, together with IRE1 and PERK. In TNF(deltaARE/+) mice with Crohn's-like ileitis, CD8αβ+ intraepithelial lymphocytes, but not CD8αα+ IELs or lamina propria lymphocytes, showed increased Grp78, ATF6, ATF4 and spliced XBP1, and UPR transducers were recruited to the granzyme B promoter in CD8αβ+ T cells. motif.name: GLIS1
evidence_context: CD8+ T-cell exhaustion in hepatocellular carcinoma; induction in psoriatic epidermis
brief_interpretation: GLIS1 is upregulated in exhausted CD8+ T cells in liver cancer and promotes exhaustion via SGK1-STAT3-PD1; it is also induced in psoriatic epidermis.
biological_interpretation: GLIS1 is a Krüppel-like zinc-finger transcription factor of the GLI-similar family. In hepatocellular carcinoma, GLIS1 was upregulated in exhausted CD8+ T cells, and its knockdown in CD8+ T cells reduced tumour growth, increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration, mitigated exhaustion and improved anti-PD1 responses in mouse and patient-derived xenograft models. Mechanistically, GLIS1 maintained PD1 expression on CD8+ T cells through transcriptional regulation of the SGK1-STAT3-PD1 pathway. Glis1 is not expressed in normal human epidermis but is induced in psoriatic epidermis and in keratinocytes treated with PMA or interferon-gamma.
